concept.name: Retest
concept.definition: The return of price to a level it has just broken, testing whether the old barrier now acts as the opposite kind — broken resistance as new support, or broken support as new resistance (the polarity principle). A successful retest is treated as confirmation of the break; a failed one warns of a false breakout.
concept.intuition: After escaping the box, price comes back to check whether the old wall now works as a floor (or ceiling) from the other side.
concept.mechanics: Observed when, following a break, price returns to the broken level and either respects it (holds beyond it, then resumes in the break direction) or fails (re-enters the old range). Many traders treat the retest, rather than the break itself, as the tradeable moment because it defines risk more tightly.
concept.failure_modes: Retests do not always occur — strong moves may never look back; and a retest that holds can still fail later, since the polarity principle is a heuristic.
concept.misconceptions: That a retest must touch the exact broken price; retests are zone affairs and may fall short or marginally overshoot the level.
concept.example: ChartSchool documents the NASDAQ 100 breaking above 935 resistance in May 1997, then falling back to test 935 as support twice before advancing to 1150.
